newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Gunshot panics Britons at Sierra Leone airport.
newsitem.headline: Gunshot panics Britons at Sierra Leone airport.

text.p: British evacuees scrambled for cover at Freetown airport on Thursday after a shot was fired during a confrontation between Nigerian and Sierra Leonean troops contesting control of the runway, witnesses said.
British diplomats confirming the incident said no one was hurt and the evacuation of 392 British and other foreign citizens went ahead as planned.

"There was a confrontation between the two sides who control opposite ends of the runway. A shot was fired as the evacuees were queuing to board the plane and everyone took defensive positions on the tarmac," a British diplomat told Reuters. He said the shot had been fired by a Sierra Leonean soldier.

Since Sunday's coup, the Sierra Leoneans have allowed the Nigerians to continue controlling the airport which has been under their care as part of regional accords over peacekeeping in neighbouring Liberia. Their relationship is described as "correct but not cordial".

Witnesses said Thursday's incident was exacerbated by the refusal of the Sierra Leoneans to allow a Nigerian C-130 Hercules to land with troops and supplies. The Nigerians insisted on landing the plane.

The evacuation flight left at 1740 GMT for London's Gatwick airport carrying Europeans, Australians, Canadians and other nationalities. Shortly after it left, two Nigerian Alpha jet fighters flew overhead.
